newsitem.title: USA: Northrop to buy Logicon for about $740 million.
newsitem.headline: Northrop to buy Logicon for about $740 million.

text.p: Aerospace giant Northrop Grumman Corp. Monday agreed to acquire Logicon Inc., a maker of advanced defence electronics and training systems, in a stock swap worth about $740 million.
The merger is aimed at positioning Northrop as a leader in the quickly growing area of defence information technology.

Northrop plans to merge Logicon, which expects revenues this year of about $560 million, with most of Northrop's Data System and Services division. The combined business would have revenues approaching $1 billion.
"This merger will firmly establish Northrop Grumman as a key player in the defence information technology arena," Northrop Grumman Chairman Kent Kresa said in a statement.
"We see continued double digit growth for this business area well into the next century."
As military budgets shrink, the nation's big weapons makers have turned more and more to electronics where profit margins are higher.

Under the terms of the deal, Logicon stockholders will receive about $52 worth of Northrop Grumman stock for each share of Logicon held. At the end of last year Logicon had about 14.3 million shares outstanding, valuing the deal at about $740 million.
The precise figure will be determined using a formula based on the average closing price for Northrop Grumman stock and can range from about $672 million to $821 million.
Logicon stock jumped $9.375 to $49.75 while Northrop Grumman sank $2.50 to $84.50, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
At $52 for each Logicon share, Northrop is paying a substantial premium. On Friday Logicon closed at $40.375, its highest level since Nov. 26 when it reached $41.375.
"It's a share exchange and there is a fairly sizable premium compared to the previous share price but it is a high quality company," said Wolfgang Demisch, an analyst at BT Securities.

"They have been a very successful and well managed software and services supplier for the U.S. government ... and the expectation is that they will continue to do well as a part of Northrop," Demisch said.
Logicon specialises in simulation, training and battle management. The company provides services that meld intelligence data to outline battle strategies.

"Historically much of the military effort was not successful because they would miss. In recent years you have gotten enough tools that most of the time you can count on the military to hit what it has aimed at," Demisch said.
"Logicion and others provide some of the tools that are necessary to make that possible."
Kresa said the acquisition reinforces Northrop's long-standing strategy is to be a leader in the areas of surveillance, precision strike and advanced battle management.
Northrop said the merger will have a minimal impact on its 1997 earnings per share.
Northrop Grumman, the nation's fifth largest military contractor, earned $234 million, or $4.33 a share, on sales of $8 billion last year.

Logicon employs about 5,000 across the United States and Western Europe. A spokesman for Northrop said no major layoffs are expected but that there will be modest job cuts from duplication of general and administrative duties.
Northrop is based in Los Angeles and Logicon is based in nearby Torrance.
The new division, which will be led by Logicon Chief Executive Jack Woodhull, will be headquartered in Torrance.
